subject: Clarifying post-breach cooperation windows and subprocessor handover
messages:
From: Olivia Turner <olivia.turner@finveo.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: security@finveo.com
Date: 2026-10-18 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident cooperation windows — next steps

Kimberly,

Thanks again for the quick sync earlier today. We had one standing ask from our legal + security teams: can you confirm Redwood's contractual obligations for evidence handover and subprocessor coordination following a confirmed data exposure? Specifically:

- The notification window (we understand your standard is 72 hours but need contract text)
- Whether Redwood will assist with cross-border forensic exports and under what conditions
- The process for on-demand access to subprocessor logs / exports and expected turnaround

FinVeo needs to reconcile the DPA language with our SOC evidence requirements. If you can point to the specific DPA clauses or provide a short summary of your operational SLA for these items, that would help our procurement and legal teams decide next steps.

Also flagging that procurement may request a tighter RTO on forensic artifacts if this is escalated.

Appreciate any attachments or a short bullets doc we can circulate.

Regards,
Olivia Turner
Head of Security Programs
FinVeo Inc.

Attachment: (none in this message)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Turner <olivia.turner@finveo.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-incident cooperation windows — next steps

Olivia — thanks for the clear list. I've pulled together a short internal plan and will share the relevant contract excerpts. High level:

- Notification: Redwood's DPA obligation is "reasonable commercial efforts" to notify within 72 hours of confirming an incident; we provide an operational escalation SLA (72 hours for initial notice, 5 business days for a preliminary forensic snapshot).
- Cross-border exports: We support forensics exports under a documented legal request; exports require review by our legal team and may need additional export controls depending on jurisdiction.
- Subprocessor access: We coordinate exports with subprocessors when we control the export; if a subprocessor controls the logs, we request that partner to provide data under previously agreed subproc terms — typical turnaround is 3–7 business days but can vary.

I'm attaching a draft forensic scope proposal and a copy of our security questionnaire (the sections you asked about are highlighted). Ben and Marissa — can you confirm whether we can commit to a 48-hour preliminary evidence snapshot as an optional procurement addendum? Jordan, please put legal on standby for any DPA redline requests.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachments: forensic-scope-proposal.pdf, security-questionnaire.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18 11:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-incident cooperation windows — next steps

Kimberly / Marissa — quick internal:

- 48h snapshot commitment: Operationally possible for hosted customers on our Supported tier if we pre-agree a runbook and evidence escrow path. For Dedicated/Private installs we'll need explicit addendum (and possibly a forensics retainer).
- Cross-border: legal review required; our standard practice is to require FinVeo execute a minimal addendum that permits export to the requested jurisdiction and indemnifies subprocessors when feasible.
- Subprocessor RTT: We can agree to a target of 72 hours for our owned services; third-party subprocessors remain variable.

I'll draft a short procurement-friendly addendum template and circulate. Marissa, can you enumerate the likely cost/retainer buckets?

—Ben
Ben Carter
Head, Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Olivia Turner <olivia.turner@finveo.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finveo.com
Date: 2026-10-18 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-incident cooperation windows — next steps

Kimberly / Ben — appreciate the draft attachments. To be transparent: FinVeo's legal counsel is pushing for two things that would materially affect procurement:

1) We need a contractual 48-hour initial evidence snapshot commitment for services handling personal data of EU residents (this will be included in our master services schedule).
2) We want Redwood to commit to coordinating subprocessor exports within 72 hours of a verified request, and to provide an escalation path to a named Redwood liaison if a subprocessor delays.

If Redwood can't sign to those windows, procurement will require a priced retainer for accelerated support. Please confirm if you can accept the 48/72 windows as a standard addendum for this account, or whether we should budget for retainer fees.

Olivia

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Turner <olivia.turner@finveo.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-19 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-incident cooperation windows — next steps

Olivia — thanks for outlining the procurement asks. I ran preliminary numbers with ops:

- 48-hour snapshot addendum (hosted): no base fee, but requires a $5k onboarding retainer + $1.2k/day for acceleration during an incident (covers engineer on-call and expedited export tooling).
- 48-hour snapshot for Dedicated/Private: depends on access model — if customer-managed network, the retainer increases to $15k and export support is limited to advisory unless we are granted temporary access.
- Subprocessor coordination SLA (72h): we can offer a contractual target plus a named liaison in the SOW; however, if a third-party refuses/needs legal process, the timeline pauses.

I'll attach the draft addendum language and the cost estimate. If FinVeo can accept the priced retainer model as an alternative, procurement can proceed faster than negotiating the tighter standard windows.

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Operations — Redwood Inference

Attachments: forensic-scope-proposal.pdf (updated), security-questionnaire.xlsx

We will need the addendum text and the named liaison (for subproc escalation) inserted into the SOW template so our counsel can sign.

- Confirmation that the 48/72 windows apply to accounts in the Hosted Supported tier under the attached SOW

If you can get the DocuSign link over, procurement will circulate immediately.

Olivia Turner

FinVeo Inc.
